findings.problem: status is a raw String instead of a domain enum. Any string value is valid, including empty strings, typos, and semantically meaningless values. The mark_sent function compares with a hardcoded literal string.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid ledger states are representable (e.g. status="sent" with is_sent=false, or status="sent" with is_validated=false). Callers can set arbitrary status values bypassing the state machine.
findings.fix: Replace `status: String` with an enum `LedgerStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }`. Remove the string field entirely and use enum variants to encode all valid states.

findings.problem: is_validated (bool) and is_sent (bool) are independent lifecycle booleans that permit impossible combinations: (false,false), (false,true), (true,false), (true,true). The state machine has no invariants.
findings.failure_mode: The type permits is_sent=true with is_validated=false (sent without validation), is_sent=false with is_validated=true (validated but not tracked as sent), and both true (ambiguous). No transition rules are enforced at the type level.
findings.fix: Replace the two booleans plus status string with a single `LedgerStatus` enum or a typestate pattern (e.g. `Ledger<S> where S: State`), so each variant owns exactly one lifecycle position with its own optional data.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> is a global Option field separate from the boolean is_sent. The timestamp can be Some(value) while is_sent is false, or None while is_sent is true. Optional lifecycle data is not owned by the variant that needs it.
findings.failure_mode: Invalid combination: sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(1234) with is_sent=false represents a ledger that has a sent timestamp but is not marked sent. This state should be impossible but the type permits it.
findings.fix: Move `sent_at: Option<u64>` into the enum variant that represents the sent state, e.g. `LedgerStatus::Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 }`. The type system guarantees the timestamp only exists when the ledger is actually sent.

findings.problem: id is a raw String with no domain meaning or validation. Any string is accepted, including empty strings, duplicates, and non-identifier values.
findings.failure_mode: Empty or malformed IDs are silently accepted. No domain validation at construction. The ID cannot carry constraints (minimum length, format) in its type.
findings.fix: Introduce a newtype `LedgerId(String)` or `LedgerId(NonEmptyString)` with a smart constructor that validates the ID on creation and returns a typed error for invalid input.

findings.problem: All four fields (id, status, is_validated, is_sent, sent_at_epoch_ms) are pub, allowing any code to construct a LedgerWorkflow with any combination of values. The struct has no smart constructor and no encapsulation.
findings.failure_mode: Any caller can create `LedgerWorkflow { id: "".into(), status: "".into(), is_validated: false, is_sent: false, sent_at_epoch_ms: None }` or any other nonsensical combination. The struct has zero invariants enforced by the type system.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide a smart constructor `LedgerWorkflow::new(id: LedgerId) -> Result<Self, LedgerError>` that initializes the struct to its only valid starting state (e.g. Pending). Remove pub fields entirely once the typestate/enum refactor is in place.

findings.problem: mark_sent returns LedgerWorkflow directly with no error type. There is no typed way to express validation failures (e.g. cannot mark a non-validated ledger as sent). The function silently accepts any state and overwrites status.
findings.failure_mode: Calling mark_sent on a validated=false ledger silently marks it sent, overwriting the status string and setting is_sent=true. No invariant check occurs. The caller has no way to know if the transition was legitimate.
findings.fix: Change the signature to `fn mark_sent(item: LedgerWorkflow) -> Result<LedgerWorkflow, LedgerError>` with a typed error enum like `LedgerError::NotValidated` and `LedgerError::AlreadySent`. Validate the precondition (is_validated=true, is_sent=false) before performing the transition.

findings.problem: mark_sent mutates the input by value and returns the struct, but the mutation is imperative field-by-field assignment rather than a pure state transition. There is no explicit state machine — the function is a bare function operating on a data bag.
findings.failure_mode: The state transition logic is hidden inside a function that operates on a struct with no type-level guarantees. Adding new states requires adding more booleans and more functions, each with their own undocumented preconditions. This makes the system unsound as it grows.
findings.fix: Define the state machine as an enum or typestate. mark_sent should operate on the state enum/typestate directly, returning a new state or a typed error. The pure transition logic belongs to the core; any I/O (logging, persistence) belongs in the shell.

findings.problem: mark_sent uses `.to_string()` to assign the status string literal, heap-allocating a new String on every call. The literal `"sent"` is already a `&'static str`.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every call to mark_sent. In a hot path or high-throughput scenario, this adds measurable pressure on the allocator and GC.
findings.fix: When refactoring to an enum, the status is eliminated entirely (zero allocations). If a string must remain, assign `&'static str` via a different field type or derive Display on the enum instead of storing a mutable String.

residual_risk: The struct represents an invalid state typestate smell: status string + lifecycle booleans + orphan lifecycle Option field. Every combination of fields is representable including impossible ones. The mark_sent function enforces zero invariants. Without the enum/typestate refactor, any future state additions will compound the problem. This is a BLOCK_GLOBAL architectural defect that must be repaired before any further delivery work on this crate.
